**Import a Minecraft world**

File ▸ Import Minecraft World… (and Import a Minecraft world… on the home screen) makes a map of a Minecraft Java world, as WorldPainter's Import ▸ Existing Minecraft map: pick its folder, or drop it, its level.dat or a region file on the window. A dialog asks for the dimension, the area (the whole world, or drawn on a map of its chunks), the heights, and what becomes of what stands above the ground: kept block for block as sculpted chunks, so buildings, trees and overhangs come back unchanged on export; trees made object layers of the world's own trees, by kind; or dropped. Each column gets its ground's height, its top block as a terrain (the map's own where one has that block on top, a new one otherwise, mods' blocks kept), its water or lava and its biome (custom biomes kept); plants, snow and carpets become ground covers, mixed grounds can become terrains that mix them, and caves can be kept too. Worlds of 1.12 and older to 26.x are read, large ones region by region with progress and cancel, and the import report lists what came in, the terrains made and the blocks left out.
